message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different branches of the mammalian tree—lions are in the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae), while zebras are in the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the two orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. In phylogenetic terms this ancestor lies within the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which contains all the major groups that split off from the ancestral lineage that gave rise to modern placental mammals.

In other words, the last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals that later diversified into the Laurasiatherian lineages (including Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, and Eulipotyphla). This ancestor lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous period.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. We need to answer. There's no tool needed. Just provide an answer. The question is about biology: lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga). They belong to different families: lions are Felidae, zebras are Equidae. Both are mammals, order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla. The common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Or maybe the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the family Felidae and Equidae. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both families. That might be the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. But the question likely expects "the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the mammalian clade that includes both families." But we can say: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and the order Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals. Actually, the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals, but more specifically the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all mammals that diverged from the same ancestor as the other Laurasiatherian orders. So the answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals. But we can mention that the last common ancestor of lions and zebras lived around 70 million years ago. So answer accordingly.
